title: MARLOW & FERN marketplace relaunch: neutralise an 8-SKU two-session product batch to one white point against an in-frame grey card, knock every product onto pure-white, vectorize the inked mark, and merge a per-SKU line sheet
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Freelancer.com brief in which a small shop wanted a product photographer to take 10-15 catalog shots of its products and also to create a logo. Two of the literal asks are outside the Adobe connector surface: it cannot operate a camera (live capture is not-available) and it cannot draw a logo from scratch (text-to-image / bespoke type design is banned). So the job is honestly re-cast as the POST-PRODUCTION half a product photographer actually does at the desk: the client sends its own raw captures and a photographed hand-inked mark, and the freelancer turns them into a matched, marketplace-ready white-background catalog set, a clean vector mark, and a merged line sheet. The un-runnable single-hero framing of the original spec is replaced by the real workload the '10-15 shots' implies: a full 8-SKU capsule shot across TWO mismatched lighting sessions, each frame carrying an in-frame 18% grey reference card so 'make the set consistent' becomes a measurable neutralisation target instead of an eyeball claim. IP: the shop is laundered to the FICTIONAL brand MARLOW & FERN (a small skincare-and-homeware label); all SKU names and copy are invented; no real marketplace is named as a requirement source (the pure-white main-image standard is described generically). Only Adobe (the tool platform) and Freelancer.com (source.platform) are named. The 8-SKU count, the two-session cast split, the in-frame grey card, the per-SKU casts, the white-point / black-point tolerances, the 1400x1400 marketplace size and the authored .indd line-sheet template are enrichment needed to make the chain concrete, failable and gradeable; nothing contradicts the source.
one_line_ask: Take eight MARLOW & FERN product photos shot across two mismatched lighting sessions (each with a grey reference card in frame), neutralise every frame to the card so the whole set reads as one white point and brightness, bring the coloured-glass and ceramic SKUs to their true matched house colours, knock every product cleanly onto a pure-white marketplace background with the sweep and card gone, vectorize the founder's inked mark, and merge one typeset line-sheet card per SKU.
full_brief:
MARLOW & FERN is a small skincare-and-homeware shop relaunching its online store and listings on the major marketplaces, and right now the catalog looks like it was shot by two different people on two different days, because it was. We are sending you our whole current capsule: eight products, one photo per SKU. Half were shot by the window on an overcast morning and half were shot later under our old work lamps, so out of camera they do not match each other at all, the whites wander all over the place, and our amber serum glass looks one colour in one shot and almost a different product in another. We dropped a standard grey balance card and a small white chip at the edge of every frame on purpose so you have an honest reference to work against, and the messy table sweep and the card are still in every shot.

What we need back:

(1) THE MATCHED SET. Every one of the eight photos corrected so its grey card reads truly neutral, with no leftover colour cast, and so the whole set sits at one consistent brightness and white point. A customer scrolling our grid must not be able to tell which shots came from which session. Carry one deliberate, restrained house look across all eight so they feel like one premium catalog, and keep it believable, no flat painted-on colour and no blown-out glass. Our coloured pieces have to land on their TRUE colours and match each other: the amber serum glass warm and rich (not muddy or greenish), our botanical-green toner glass a true deep green (not yellowed), and our terracotta candle vessel warm but calm, not glowing or radioactive. Neutral products (the frosted cream jar, the matte-white pump, the kraft soap box, the brass-lidded balm tin, the clear roller) must simply read clean and true, whites believable, darks not crushed.

(2) MARKETPLACE PACKSHOTS. Each product lifted cleanly off its cluttered sweep and set on a pure solid-white (#FFFFFF) background, delivered as a square 1400x1400 marketplace image with the product centred and the sweep and grey card gone. This is the hard standard the marketplaces enforce for a main image, so the white has to be genuinely white with no grey cast and no halo or hard cardboard edge around the product. Retain a card-bearing corrected master of each frame as well, so we can eyeball the whole set against the cards, but the marketplace images themselves must have the card cropped out.

(3) THE MARK. Turn the founder's photographed hand-inked brand mark (a botanical fern-sprig emblem with our hand-lettered name beneath it, shot on off-white paper at a slight angle) into a clean, infinitely scalable vector so it works from a favicon to a shop-front sign, edges crisp at any size.

(4) THE LINE SHEET. Using the InDesign line-sheet template and the SKU sheet we are sending, produce one finished product card per SKU with its cleaned packshot placed and its name, variant, size and price set in type. One card per product.

DELIVERY: hand back the eight card-bearing corrected masters as our contact set, the eight marketplace packshots, the vector mark, the merged line sheet, and a short note telling us, per photo, exactly what white-balance and exposure correction you landed on and what you did to the coloured pieces, so we can trust the set is genuinely matched and not just eyeballed.

inputs.name: MF01_amber_serum_bottle.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal ecommerce product photo, raw unretouched DSLR look, a single amber-glass cosmetic serum bottle with a black dropper cap standing upright on a slightly scuffed light wooden table used as a makeshift sweep, blank unlabelled amber glass (no legible text or logo). A standard 18% neutral grey balance card and a small white chip rest flat on the table at the lower-left edge of the frame as a white-balance reference. Shot under COOL overcast window light with a distinct blue-cyan cast, slightly flat and marginally under-exposed as if straight off the camera. Real glass reflections and a soft specular highlight on the curved shoulder, real wood grain, faint soft contact shadow. 3:2 landscape, 4000x2667px, candid documentary, no text overlays, not CGI-glossy.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU MF-01, Session A (cool/blue, session 1 of two). COLOURED-GLASS SKU: the cool cast pushes the amber toward a muddy olive-green, so after the grey-card neutralisation (WARM the temperature, lift exposure slightly, tint off green) a masked luminosity-preserving HSL pass must rotate the amber back off green to a true warm amber and set it to the shared house-amber target so it MATCHES nothing-else-yet but establishes one of the true colours. The in-frame grey card is the neutralisation ground truth; a single WB copied across all eight leaves this frame cold. The soft specular on the glass must not be pushed to clip.

inputs.name: MF02_green_toner_bottle.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal ecommerce product photo, raw unretouched look, a botanical deep-green glass toner bottle with a matte black pump, blank unlabelled glass, standing on the same light wooden table sweep. A standard 18% neutral grey balance card and a small white chip sit on the table at the lower-right edge of the frame. Shot under WARM tungsten work-lamp light with a strong orange cast and slightly bright exposure. Real green-glass translucency and a bright reflection down one side, faint soft contact shadow. 3:2 landscape, 4000x2667px, candid documentary, no text, not CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU MF-02, Session B (warm/orange, session 2). COLOURED-GLASS SKU and the OPPOSITE corrective sign to MF-01: the grey-card neutralisation here COOLS the temperature and pulls exposure DOWN. The warm cast has pushed the green toward khaki-yellow, so the masked HSL pass rotates the green back off yellow toward a true deep botanical green at the shared house-green target. Proves per-frame direction: MF-01 warms, MF-02 cools; one shared WB cannot serve both. Watch the bright side reflection so the green does not clip.

inputs.name: MF03_terracotta_candle_vessel.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal ecommerce product photo, raw unretouched look, a terracotta / rust-clay ceramic candle vessel with a natural soy candle inside, unlit, matte glazed clay, standing on the light wooden table sweep. A standard 18% neutral grey balance card and a small white chip at the frame edge. Shot under WARM tungsten work-lamp light with an orange cast; the already-saturated terracotta glaze is pushed near-glowing and slightly clipping on the brightest curve. Real clay glaze texture and soft pooling shadow, faint contact shadow. 3:2 landscape, 4000x2667px, candid documentary, no text, not CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU MF-03, Session B (warm). COLOURED SKU and the OVER-CORRECTION trap: unlike the two glass SKUs, the correct masked pass here RESTRAINS the terracotta (pull saturation down and drop the luminance of the hottest curve) so it stops glowing and clipping and lands on the true calm house terracotta. A blanket 'make the colours pop' vibrance boost, or copying the olive/green rotate move, sends it radioactive. Tests per-hue reasoning: two coloured SKUs get boosted/rotated to true, this one gets pulled back.

inputs.name: MF04_frosted_cream_jar.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal ecommerce product photo, raw unretouched look, a frosted-white glass cream jar with a pale wooden lid, blank unlabelled, standing on the light wooden table sweep. A standard 18% neutral grey balance card and a small white chip at the lower edge of the frame. Shot under COOL overcast window light with a blue-cyan cast, flat exposure. Real frosted-glass surface scatter and soft folds of shadow, faint contact shadow, low contrast between the near-white jar and the pale sweep. 3:2 landscape, 4000x2667px, candid documentary, no text, not CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU MF-04, Session A (cool). NEUTRAL near-white RESTRAINT case: warm to neutralise the card WITHOUT tinting the frosted white grey or blue, and do not clip the frosted white to 255. Low jar-to-sweep contrast makes the knockout an isolation-edge case that a luminance guess fails. No colour-truth pass needed.

inputs.name: MF05_matte_white_pump_bottle.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal ecommerce product photo, raw unretouched look, a matte-white lotion pump bottle, blank unlabelled, standing on the light wooden table sweep. A standard 18% neutral grey balance card and a small white chip at the frame edge. Shot under WARM tungsten work-lamp light with an orange cast, slightly bright exposure. Real matte plastic surface, soft even reflection, faint contact shadow, low contrast between the white bottle and the sweep. 3:2 landscape, 4000x2667px, candid documentary, no text, not CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU MF-05, Session B (warm). NEUTRAL near-white RESTRAINT case, opposite session to MF-04: cool to neutral and pull brightness down to the shared exposure WITHOUT driving the matte white blue-grey and without clipping. Another low-contrast white-on-white isolation edge for the knockout. No colour-truth pass.

inputs.name: MF06_brass_lidded_balm_tin.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal ecommerce product photo, raw unretouched look, a small dark bronze / charcoal-metal balm tin with a brushed brass lid, blank unlabelled, standing on the light wooden table sweep. A standard 18% neutral grey balance card and a small white chip at the frame edge. Shot under COOL overcast window light, flat and slightly under-exposed so the dark tin body muddies toward black. Real brushed-metal micro-scratches and a soft brass highlight, faint contact shadow. 3:2 landscape, 4000x2667px, candid documentary, no text, not CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU MF-06, Session A (cool, dark/under). NEUTRAL BLACK-POINT discipline: warm to neutral against the card and LIFT exposure to the set brightness while holding the black point so the dark tin body stays a rich charcoal, not crushed to 0 and not washed to grey; keep the brass highlight off clipping. Its dark edge cuts cleanly against the white sweep, the easy isolation of the batch, contrast with the near-white SKUs. No colour-truth pass.

inputs.name: MF07_kraft_soap_box.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal ecommerce product photo, raw unretouched look, a kraft-brown cardboard soap box, blank unlabelled recycled kraft paper, standing on the light wooden table sweep. A standard 18% neutral grey balance card and a small white chip at the frame edge. Shot under COOL overcast window light with a faint blue cast, gentle exposure. Real kraft paper fibre texture and crisp box edges, faint contact shadow. 3:2 landscape, 4000x2667px, candid documentary, no text, not CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU MF-07, Session A (cool). NEUTRAL mid-tone case: warm to neutralise the card while keeping the kraft brown a believable warm tan, not orange and not greyed; its crisp box edges isolate cleanly. Its warm-brown hue is close to the terracotta SKU but the correct answer is DIFFERENT: cast-neutralisation only, no chroma restraint, so the two warm-reddish objects must not be blanket-treated the same. No colour-truth pass.

inputs.name: MF08_clear_glass_roller.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal ecommerce product photo, raw unretouched look, a small clear-glass roller bottle with a stainless roller ball and a pale cap, blank unlabelled clear glass showing the sweep through it, standing on the light wooden table sweep. A standard 18% neutral grey balance card and a small white chip at the frame edge. Shot under WARM tungsten work-lamp light with an orange cast, slightly bright. Real glass refraction and bright edge speculars, faint contact shadow, the transparent body is low-contrast against the sweep. 3:2 landscape, 4000x2667px, candid documentary, no text, not CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU MF-08, Session B (warm). NEUTRAL restraint + hardest transparent isolation edge: cool to neutral against the card and protect the bright glass speculars from clipping. The clear glass reads through to the sweep so the knockout must isolate the whole bottle silhouette as the semantic foreground (not a luminance threshold) and set it on solid white; the see-through body is the outer silhouette, NOT an enclosed interior hole, so remove_background handles it. No colour-truth pass.

inputs.name: MF_founder_mark_sketch.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A phone photograph of a rough hand-inked brand mark on slightly off-white textured paper: a single botanical fern-sprig emblem curving into a small circle, drawn in dark grey-black fineliner ink with imperfect line weight and a couple of stray pencil guide lines, and the hand-lettered words 'MARLOW & FERN' beneath it in rough capitals. The paper is shot at a slight angle under indoor lighting with a faint shadow in one corner and a subtly uneven grey-ish cast (not pure-white paper). Visible paper grain and tiny smudges. High resolution, long edge about 3000px. No digital cleanup, looks like a real founder's napkin-style sketch.
inputs.realism_notes: The vector-mark source, and a genuine PREP-BEFORE-TRACE case. The mark is shot on greyish paper at an angle with stray guide lines, so a naive trace of the raw file returns garbage paths and a stray border. The honest chain is auto_straighten, then crisp the ink with contrast, then drop the paper to transparency, then crop to the mark's tight bounds, THEN vectorize, so image_vectorize sees a clean prepared raster. The hand-lettered wordmark has enclosed counters (A, R, O) which the knock-to-white leaves filled white, fine for the light/white grounds this mark is used on (webstore header, line sheet); no dark-ground knockout is claimed. gemini-3-pro-image because the sketch carries legible hand-lettered type.

inputs.name: marlow_fern_linesheet.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED asset (client-supplied, not model-generated): a genuine single-page InDesign line-sheet card template, ~4x6 in at 300 DPI plus 0.125 in bleed, with a product-image frame carrying an @-prefixed image-path variable (@packshot) and live text merge fields <<product_name>>, <<variant>>, <<size>>, <<price>>, plus the MARLOW & FERN mark placed as static masthead furniture. Built as a real .indd bound to a data-merge source so document_merge_data_layout binds one card per row.
inputs.realism_notes: Supplied so the composed endpoint is real: a genuine authored .indd with live <<fields>> AND an @-image column is the only connector-legal way to place a produced image into a laid-out page. The template layout is the client's; the distinctive quality of each finished card, the matched true colour and the clean white knockout of the placed packshot, is the agent's work. document_merge_data_vector is the WRONG tool (text-only, cannot bind @packshot); a convert_pdf_to_indd target would not bind fields. Mirrors the supplied-template pattern used by the passing exemplars.

inputs.name: marlow_fern_skus.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED asset (client-supplied): an 8-row data-merge CSV, one row per SKU (MF-01..MF-08), with text columns product_name, variant, size, price and an @-prefixed image-path column (@packshot) whose cells must resolve to the eight pure-white marketplace packshots the agent produces. Header names match the <<fields>> in the .indd template.
inputs.realism_notes: The @packshot column is the binding contract: the agent must point each cell at its own produced 1400x1400 white-background packshot so document_merge_data_layout places each cleaned product on its card. Row count = 8 fixes the page=row acceptance gate. Text-only document_merge_data_vector cannot bind the image column and is the wrong tool here.

outputs.name: corrected_masters_x8
outputs.spec: The eight card-BEARING corrected masters as one matched contact set (MF-01..MF-08): each neutralised to its own in-frame 18% grey card and carried to ONE shared house white point and brightness across the whole batch, with the three coloured SKUs (amber serum, green toner, terracotta vessel) brought to their true matched house colours via masked luminosity-preserving HSL. The grey card is RETAINED in every frame in this deliverable so neutrality is gradeable. Full-res PNG (~4000x2667). ACCEPTANCE (grader-checked on this card-bearing set): each frame's grey card reads visually neutral, R,G,B within roughly 3 levels of channel spread; the card mid-grey sits within roughly 4 levels of a common target across all eight; no channel clipped to 255 or crushed to 0. DELIVERABLE 1.

outputs.name: marketplace_packshots_x8
outputs.spec: The eight marketplace packshots (MF-01..MF-08): each corrected product lifted off its sweep and set on a pure solid-white #FFFFFF background via image_remove_background({backgroundColor:#FFFFFF}), with the sweep AND the grey card gone, a clean product edge and no halo, then cropped/resized to a centred square 1400x1400 px, sRGB PNG. ACCEPTANCE (grader-checked on this delivered set): background is uniform #FFFFFF; the grey card is EXCLUDED from frame (card neutrality is graded on corrected_masters_x8, card exclusion is checked here, on separate files); interior/see-through space is not solid-filled; downscaled from the 4000x2667 source, never upscaled. DELIVERABLE 2.

outputs.name: marlow_fern_mark.svg
outputs.spec: The MARLOW & FERN hand-inked mark (fern-sprig emblem + hand-lettered wordmark) traced to a clean scalable SVG with crisp paths, favicon-to-signage safe, produced by prep-before-trace: auto-straighten, crisp the ink, drop the paper to transparency, crop to bounds, THEN image_vectorize. For light/white grounds (webstore header, line sheet); enclosed counters read white. DELIVERABLE 3.

outputs.name: linesheet_x8_pdf
outputs.spec: The eight-SKU line sheet, ONE card per CSV row, produced by merging marlow_fern_skus.csv into the authored marlow_fern_linesheet.indd via document_merge_data_layout: each card places that SKU's 1400x1400 white-background packshot through the @packshot image column and typesets <<product_name>>, <<variant>>, <<size>>, <<price>>. ACCEPTANCE gate: card/page count == data row count == 8 (a broken or empty-frame merge fails this); each placed packshot renders at >=300 DPI at the card's image-frame trim. The 'hero' is simply page 1 of the merged PDF. DELIVERABLE 4.

outputs.name: correction_params_report
outputs.spec: A short accompanying note (secondary to the images, NOT the primary deliverable) in which the agent reports, per image: the corrective white-balance move made to hit the grey card (temperature and tint direction/magnitude), the exposure delta, and for the three coloured SKUs the masked HSL colour-truth move (hue/sat/luminance) applied, plus a one-line confirmation that each frame's grey card reads neutral and lands on the common mid-grey target. This makes 'matched to the card' verifiable rather than asserted. It is an applied-settings log the agent knows because it set them, NOT a measured/read pixel value.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: MF01_amber_serum_bottle.jpg, MF02_green_toner_bottle.jpg, MF03_terracotta_candle_vessel.jpg, MF04_frosted_cream_jar.jpg, MF05_matte_white_pump_bottle.jpg, MF06_brass_lidded_balm_tin.jpg, MF07_kraft_soap_box.jpg, MF08_clear_glass_roller.jpg, MF_founder_mark_sketch.jpg, marlow_fern_linesheet.indd, marlow_fern_skus.csv
connector_workflow.note: Load the eight product photos, the founder's mark sketch, the authored .indd line-sheet template and the SKU CSV into the working project in one batch so every downstream step runs against real asset references. Single upload, plumbing, not counted as difficulty.

Neutralise MF-01 to its in-frame grey card so the card reads truly neutral and the frame reaches the shared house white point and brightness, then lay the shared restrained house-look tonal constants. The temperature/tint/exposure delta is specific to THIS frame's capture and the agent reasons it from the card, not a batch constant. Hold the glass specular off clipping. Records the applied settings for the params note.
Semantically select the amber serum glass so the colour-truth adjustment is confined to the product and never touches the grey card, white chip or sweep. Returns a maskURI.

Masked luminosity-preserving HSL on the amber glass: carry it to the true shared house-amber target (bounded hue nudge plus saturation/luminance set) so the coloured pieces read true and matched. The existing luminosity carries the glass reflections; this is an authored look the agent reasons to, not a preset, not auto-tone, not whole-image color_overlay. Card-bearing corrected master for the contact set.

Lift MF-01 off its sweep and set it on a pure solid-white ground via image_remove_background with backgroundColor #FFFFFF. This is the connector-legal knockout: it isolates the product as the foreground, keeps the edge and any see-through space clean, and removes the sweep AND the grey card in one move. Deliberately NOT select_subject/select_by_prompt -> invert_selection -> image_fill_area, which solids a flat plate, halos the edge and bricks see-through space.

Crop/resize the white-ground MF-01 to a centred square 1400x1400 marketplace image, card out of frame, sRGB. Downscale/reframe of the 4000x2667 source only, never canvas-extend or upscale. Feeds the packshots deliverable and MF-01's @packshot cell.

Neutralise MF-02 to its in-frame grey card to the shared white point and brightness, then lay the shared house-look constants. This frame's WB/exposure delta is its own, reasoned from the card, and is not the same as MF-01's, applying one correction to the whole batch fails the card. Hold the bright side reflection off clipping. Records the applied settings.
Semantically select the green toner glass only so the colour-truth pass never touches the card, chip or sweep. Returns a maskURI.

Masked luminosity-preserving HSL on the green glass: carry it to the true shared house-green target (bounded hue rotation plus saturation/luminance set) so it reads a true deep botanical green and matches the set's colour discipline. Authored, luminosity-preserving, not a preset or whole-image overlay. Card-bearing corrected master for the contact set.

Set MF-02 on a pure solid-white ground via image_remove_background({backgroundColor:#FFFFFF}); sweep and card removed, edge clean. Same anti-pattern avoidance as MF-01 (no select -> invert -> fill_area).
Crop/resize white-ground MF-02 to centred square 1400x1400, card out, sRGB, downscale only. Feeds the packshots deliverable and MF-02's @packshot cell.

Neutralise MF-03 to its in-frame grey card to the shared white point and brightness, then lay the shared house-look constants, protecting the already-hot glaze from clipping before the colour-truth pass. This frame's WB/exposure delta is its own. Records the applied settings.
Semantically select the terracotta ceramic vessel only so the colour-truth pass is confined to the product. Returns a maskURI.

Masked luminosity-preserving HSL on the terracotta glaze: bring it to the true calm house terracotta. The correct move here is RESTRAINT (pull saturation down and drop the luminance of the hottest curve) so it stops glowing, the opposite direction to the two glass SKUs, which is why per-hue reasoning matters rather than a blanket colour boost. Card-bearing corrected master for the contact set.
Set MF-03 on a pure solid-white ground via image_remove_background({backgroundColor:#FFFFFF}); sweep and card removed. No select -> invert -> fill_area.
Crop/resize white-ground MF-03 to centred square 1400x1400, card out, sRGB, downscale only. Feeds the packshots deliverable and MF-03's @packshot cell.

Neutralise MF-04 to its in-frame grey card to the shared white point and brightness and lay the shared house-look constants. Restraint case: hold the near-white product believable, no colour tint and no clipping. No colour-truth pass, so this neutralised frame IS the card-bearing corrected master. This frame's WB/exposure delta is its own; records the applied settings.

Set MF-04 on a pure solid-white ground via image_remove_background({backgroundColor:#FFFFFF}); the low product-to-sweep contrast makes this an isolation-edge case the semantic foreground isolation handles, where a luminance guess would fail. Sweep and card removed. No select -> invert -> fill_area.
Crop/resize white-ground MF-04 to centred square 1400x1400, card out, sRGB, downscale only. Feeds the packshots deliverable and MF-04's @packshot cell.

Neutralise MF-05 to its in-frame grey card to the shared white point and brightness and lay the shared house-look constants. Restraint case, opposite session to MF-04: pull brightness to the shared target while keeping the matte white believable and off clipping. No colour-truth pass; this frame IS its card-bearing corrected master. Own WB/exposure delta; records the applied settings.

Set MF-05 on a pure solid-white ground via image_remove_background({backgroundColor:#FFFFFF}); another low-contrast white-on-white edge, handled by semantic foreground isolation. Sweep and card removed. No select -> invert -> fill_area.
Crop/resize white-ground MF-05 to centred square 1400x1400, card out, sRGB, downscale only. Feeds the packshots deliverable and MF-05's @packshot cell.

Neutralise MF-06 to its in-frame grey card to the shared white point and brightness and lay the shared house-look constants. Black-point discipline: lift exposure to the set brightness while holding the black point so the dark tin stays a rich charcoal, not crushed to 0 and not washed to grey; keep the brass highlight off clipping. No colour-truth pass; this frame IS its card-bearing corrected master. Own WB/exposure delta; records the applied settings.

Set MF-06 on a pure solid-white ground via image_remove_background({backgroundColor:#FFFFFF}); the dark tin edge cuts cleanly against the sweep, the easy isolation of the batch. Sweep and card removed. No select -> invert -> fill_area.
Crop/resize white-ground MF-06 to centred square 1400x1400, card out, sRGB, downscale only. Feeds the packshots deliverable and MF-06's @packshot cell.

Neutralise MF-07 to its in-frame grey card to the shared white point and brightness and lay the shared house-look constants. Mid-tone case: keep the kraft brown a believable warm tan, not orange and not greyed; cast-neutralisation only, no chroma restraint (its warm-brown hue looks near the terracotta SKU but the correct treatment is different). No colour-truth pass; this frame IS its card-bearing corrected master. Own WB/exposure delta; records the applied settings.
Set MF-07 on a pure solid-white ground via image_remove_background({backgroundColor:#FFFFFF}); crisp box edges isolate cleanly. Sweep and card removed. No select -> invert -> fill_area.
Crop/resize white-ground MF-07 to centred square 1400x1400, card out, sRGB, downscale only. Feeds the packshots deliverable and MF-07's @packshot cell.

Neutralise MF-08 to its in-frame grey card to the shared white point and brightness and lay the shared house-look constants. Restraint case: protect the bright glass speculars from clipping. No colour-truth pass; this frame IS its card-bearing corrected master. Own WB/exposure delta; records the applied settings.

Set MF-08 on a pure solid-white ground via image_remove_background({backgroundColor:#FFFFFF}); the transparent body is the outer silhouette (not an enclosed interior hole), isolated as the semantic foreground against the low-contrast sweep. Sweep and card removed. No select -> invert -> fill_area.

Crop/resize white-ground MF-08 to centred square 1400x1400, card out, sRGB, downscale only. Feeds the packshots deliverable and MF-08's @packshot cell. Steps 6/11/16/19/22/25/28/31 are marketplace_packshots_x8 and the eight @packshot cells; the mf__master outputs are corrected_masters_x8.
Prep-before-trace, step 1: level the mark sketch photographed at a slight angle so the traced paths are not skewed. Consumes the uploaded sketch.
Prep-before-trace, step 2: crisp the grey-ish ink against the off-white paper with contrast/exposure so the trace sees a clean high-contrast mark, not a muddy pencil-grey field. Consumes step 32.
Prep-before-trace, step 3: drop the paper to transparency so only the ink mark remains. Consumes step 33.
Prep-before-trace, step 4: trim to the mark's tight bounds so vectorize spends its resolution on the emblem and lettering, not empty canvas, and no stray border path is traced. Consumes step 34.

Trace the prepared raster mark to a clean scalable SVG with crisp paths, favicon-to-signage safe. DELIVERABLE 3. Tracing the raw angled greyish photo instead (skipping the prep) returns garbage paths and a stray border; the prep chain is what makes this honest. Consumes step 35.

chaining_note: One batch upload (1) fans into eight parallel per-SKU chains that converge on a genuine composed endpoint. The three coloured SKUs run a five-step chain: image_apply_adjustments neutralises the frame to its in-frame grey card and lays the shared house-look constants (WB/exposure delta per frame, tonal shape constant); image_select_by_prompt masks the product; image_adjust_hsl carries the colour to a shared house target; image_remove_background({backgroundColor:#FFFFFF}) sets it on pure white; image_crop_and_resize makes the 1400x1400 packshot (MF-01 2-6, MF-02 7-11, MF-03 12-16). The five neutral SKUs run a three-step chain: neutralise (which IS the card-bearing master, no colour-truth pass) -> remove_background({backgroundColor:#FFFFFF}) -> crop_and_resize (MF-04 17-19, MF-05 20-22, MF-06 23-25, MF-07 26-28, MF-08 29-31). The mf__master outputs form corrected_masters_x8 (card retained); the mf__packshot outputs form marketplace_packshots_x8 (card cropped out) and the eight @packshot cells. The mark runs a prep-before-trace chain: auto_straighten (32) -> apply_adjustments crisp (33) -> remove_background paper-to-transparent (34) -> crop_to_bounds (35) -> vectorize (36) => marlow_fern_mark.svg. Finally document_merge_data_layout (37) binds the CSV + the eight packshots into the authored .indd, one card per row (8 pages). Every post-upload step consumes a named prior output; the merge converges all eight packshot chains plus the template and CSV. 37 calls, 10 distinct Adobe tools, one upload and no folder/copy padding.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon product_ecom_whitebg rebuild of the amputated single-hero original: 37 connector calls, 10 distinct Adobe tools, one batch upload fanning into eight dependent per-SKU chains plus a prep-before-trace mark chain that converge on a genuine composed endpoint (an authored-.indd data merge). Difficulty is DEPTH, not repetition: the eight neutralisations are NOT one recipe run eight times, each is a per-image WB/exposure delta whose SIGN flips by shooting session (cool session-A frames warm up, warm session-B frames cool down) and whose magnitude the agent reasons to from the in-frame grey card, so applying one correction to all eight visibly fails the match at the cards. On top sit three heterogeneous masked colour-truth decisions in DIFFERENT directions (rotate the amber back off green and the toner back off yellow to true saturated house targets; RESTRAIN the terracotta so it stops clipping) plus restraint cases on the near-white/matte-white/clear-glass frames, black-point discipline on the dark tin, and a low-contrast white-on-white isolation edge. The white background is a solid #FFFFFF via remove_background({backgroundColor}), NOT the select -> invert -> fill_area plate anti-pattern (which was in the original spec and is deliberately removed). The mark is vectorized only after a real prep-before-trace chain. The endpoint is a genuine @-image-column merge (text-only vector merge and PDF-converted .indd both fail to bind), gated on page-count==row-count and >=300 DPI. Every step is a headless [C] connector call: no generative fill/expand, no compositing, no upscaling, no layout-by-coordinates, no from-scratch logo drawing.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (wrong DECISION, not a self-measurement): every frame carries an in-frame 18% grey card and the acceptance test is that each card reads truly neutral (~3 levels of channel spread) with its mid-grey within ~4 levels of a common target across all eight, and the agent must REPORT its per-image temperature/tint/exposure move, so a naive agent that copies one white-balance across the two-session batch leaves the cool frames cold and the warm frames warm and is caught at the cards. HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: (1) cross-asset consistency to a measurable target across eight products shot under two opposite casts, including bringing the amber and green glass to true matched house colours and holding the near-white/matte-white/clear pieces believable while neutralising, and holding the dark tin's black point, which a novice cannot match by eye; (2) constraint-reasoning around tool limits, the white knockout via remove_background({backgroundColor:#FFFFFF}) not select->invert->fill_area, the colour-truth via the only masked path image_adjust_hsl not whole-image color_overlay or flat fill_area, image placement only via a genuine @-image-column .indd merge, and prep-before-trace discipline on the mark. THE TRAP: the brief's 'put every product on pure white' invites the select_by_prompt/select_subject -> invert_selection -> image_fill_area plate chain, which looks right but solid-fills a flat white plate with a hard halo and destroys see-through/soft edges (the exact chain the original spec used and this rebuild removes); a second trap is copying one WB/exposure across all eight, which the two-session cast split guarantees will not match; a third is over-boosting saturation so the terracotta goes radioactive or blanket-treating it like the kraft box; a fourth is tracing the raw angled greyish mark photo instead of prepping it, which returns garbage paths; a fifth is cropping the grey card out BEFORE neutralising, destroying the reference. MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE: on corrected_masters_x8 (card retained) each grey card neutral within ~3 levels of channel spread and its mid-grey within ~4 levels of the common target with no channel clipped; on marketplace_packshots_x8 the background is uniform #FFFFFF, the card is excluded, and the crop is a downscale to 1400x1400; the mark is a clean SVG; the merged line sheet has card-count == row-count == 8 at >=300 DPI at trim; and a per-image parameter report so 'matched to the card' is verifiable rather than asserted.
